title: Leibniz's monadology of observing entities

tellings.quote: Now this is something that Livinets suggested back in 1700. He had this monodology

plain: The philosopher Leibniz proposed that reality is made of countless observing entities, which he called monads, and he set out the idea in a work called the Monadology. A researcher named Don Hoffman brings this up on the show and dates it to around 1700: "this is something that Livinets suggested back in 1700. He had this monodology." Hoffman uses it to show that his own idea, a universe built from minds that observe, has very old roots.
